newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bear Stearns sees Cardoso hurt by municipal vote.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns sees Cardoso hurt by municipal vote.

text.p: The outcome of Brazil's municipal ballot last week hurt President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, splintering his support in Congress and damaging his re-election bid, Bear Stearns & Co said in a report.
"We assess (Thursday's) elections outcome as being slightly negative for President Cardoso," the investment bank said.

The right-wing Liberal Front Party (PFL), a key Cardoso ally in Congress, posted excellent results and will now have greater leverage to water down planned reforms, principally the government's plans to curb state autonomy, it said.
"Key to watch will be what Cardoso has to give up in exchange for support," Bear Stearns said.

The investment bank added it doubts Cardoso, who is seeking a constitutional amendment to allow him to run again in 1998, will risk damaging the stabilization plan or the economy as it could wreck his re-election chances.

Bear Stearns also said Cardoso's Social Democratic (PSDB) party fared poorly in the nationwide vote while Sao Paulo mayor and likely presidential hopeful, Paulo Maluf, was strengthened by the strong showing of his hand-picked candidate, Celso Pitta.

Apart from the PFL and Maluf's Progressive Party (PPB), the elections also were a boon for the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), the country's largest party and a lukewarm Cardoso ally, the report said.
"The PMDB was apparently so pleased with their performance across the country that they are considering having their own candidate for 1998," Bear Stearns said.
